newsitem.title: USA: Famed designer Jean Louis dies in California.
newsitem.headline: Famed designer Jean Louis dies in California.

text.p: Oscar-winning costume designer Jean Louis, who made dresses for former First Lady Nancy Reagan, Marilyn Monroe and a bevy of Hollywood stars including his wife Loretta Young, has died, the Los Angeles Times reported on Wednesday. He was 89.
The newspaper quoted an undertaker as saying the French-born Louis died on Sunday at his home in the fashionable California desert town of Palm Springs.
Louis, born Jean Louis Berthault, won the Academy Award in 1956 for costume design for the movie "The Solid Gold Cadillac." He donated the gold statuette to a museum in his native Paris.

He designed costumes for more than 60 films and was nominated for Oscars 14 times for such movies as "From Here to Eternity," A Star is Born," "Pal Joey," "Judgment at Nuremberg" and "Thoroughly Modern Millie."
His gowns were worn by about 200 of Hollywood's most glamorous women, including Rita Hayworth, Judy Garland and Julie Andrews, as well as the Duchess of Windsor.
His "see-through" gowns for Marlene Dietrich's Las Vegas shows shocked the world in the 1950's, making the German star appear nude and covered with only jewels and fur.

Louis also designed the heavily beaded gown that Marilyn Monroe wore for her famed rendition of "Happy Birthday" to late President John Kennedy in Washington. The dress now hangs in the Smithsonian Institution.

Mrs Reagan, a former actress, considered Louis among her favourite American designers and wore a Louis creation -- a simple black silk jacquard dress -- the night her husband was first elected president in 1980.
The designer's career began at the Agnes Drecoll Place Vendome in Paris but it took off in the United States after he visited New York on vacation in 1935.
He is survived by his wife and a brother, Adrian Berthault, in Paris.
